```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Prepares the *Student's Dropout and Academic Success* dataset (4424 students, 36 variables + `Target`: Dropout / Enrolled / Graduate).
Output: train / validation / test sets (60/20/20) saved in `data/prepared_data.rds`, used by `02_models.Rmd`.
References to chapters point to the thesis PDF (Chapter 6.3 for variable selection, 7.1 for the split).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
```

# Data

Load the dataset (semicolon-separated CSV).

```{r}
# NOTE: replace with the path to the dataset on your machine
data <- read.csv("data/data.csv", sep = ";", header = T)
```

# Variable selection and feature engineering

Merge the highly correlated 1st- and 2nd-semester variables (credited, enrolled, approved; |corr| > 0.85) into three yearly totals, then drop the original six.

```{r}
data$tot_units_credited <- rowSums(data[,c(22, 28)], na.rm = TRUE)
data$tot_units_enrolled <- rowSums(data[,c(23, 29)], na.rm = TRUE)
# data$tot_units_evaluation <- rowSums(data[,c(24, 30)], na.rm = TRUE)
data$tot_num_units_approved <- rowSums(data[,c(25, 31)], na.rm = TRUE)
# data$tot_year_grade <- rowMeans(data[,c(26, 32)], na.rm = TRUE)
# data$tot_units_no_eval <- rowSums(data[,c(27, 33)], na.rm = TRUE)
data_new <- data[,-c(22, 23, 25, 28, 29, 31)]
```

Drop variables that are not informative according to the boxplots (macroeconomic variables, units without evaluation, total units credited).

```{r}
data_new <- data_new[,-c(32,24,27,28,29,30)]
```

# Categorical variables with many levels

Count the levels of the parents' qualification and occupation variables.

```{r}
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Mother.s.qualification)))
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Father.s.qualification)))
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Mother.s.occupation)))
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Father.s.occupation)))
```

Merge rare levels into a single level "Altro" ("Other") and drop unused levels.
Father's variables: levels with at most 2 observations are merged. Mother's variables: the threshold is `< 1`, so no level is merged.

```{r}
rare_levels <- names(which(table(data_new$Father.s.occupation) <= 2))

# Step 2: Merge rare levels into a single level called "Altro" ("Other")
data_new$Father.s.occupation <- factor(ifelse(data_new$Father.s.occupation %in% rare_levels, 
                                           "Altro", 
                                           as.character(data_new$Father.s.occupation)))

# Step 3: Remove unused levels
data_new$Father.s.occupation <- droplevels(data_new$Father.s.occupation)
rare_levels <- names(which(table(data_new$Mother.s.occupation) < 1))

# Step 2: Merge rare levels into a single level called "Altro" ("Other")
data_new$Mother.s.occupation <- factor(ifelse(data_new$Mother.s.occupation %in% rare_levels, 
                                           "Altro", 
                                           as.character(data_new$Mother.s.occupation)))

# Step 3: Remove unused levels
data_new$Mother.s.occupation <- droplevels(data_new$Mother.s.occupation)

rare_levels <- names(which(table(data_new$Father.s.qualification) <= 2))

# Step 2: Merge rare levels into a single level called "Altro" ("Other")
data_new$Father.s.qualification <- factor(ifelse(data_new$Father.s.qualification %in% rare_levels, 
                                           "Altro", 
                                           as.character(data_new$Father.s.qualification)))

# Step 3: Remove unused levels
data_new$Father.s.qualification <- droplevels(data_new$Father.s.qualification)

rare_levels <- names(which(table(data_new$Mother.s.qualification) < 1))

# Step 2: Merge rare levels into a single level called "Altro" ("Other")
data_new$Mother.s.qualification <- factor(ifelse(data_new$Mother.s.qualification %in% rare_levels, 
                                           "Altro", 
                                           as.character(data_new$Mother.s.qualification)))

# Step 3: Remove unused levels
data_new$Mother.s.qualification <- droplevels(data_new$Mother.s.qualification)
```

Check the number of levels again after merging.

```{r}
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Mother.s.qualification)))
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Father.s.qualification)))
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Mother.s.occupation)))
length(levels(as.factor(data_new$Father.s.occupation)))
```

Split numerical and categorical variables, then put the numerical ones first.
The final dataset has 27 predictors; `Target` is the last column.

```{r}
data_numerical <- data_new[,c(7,13,20,22,23,24,25,27,28)]
data_categorical <- data_new[,- c(7,13,20,22,23,24,25,27,28)]
#data_numerical <- scale(data_numerical)
data_new <- cbind(data_numerical, data_categorical) # the target is the last column
```

# Optional: pre-enrollment dataset (Chapter 9)

Keep only information available at enrollment (drops the academic performance variables and "Tuition fees up to date", which are only known after the start of university).
Disabled by default: set `eval=TRUE` to build the pre-enrollment dataset, and change the output file name in the last chunk to avoid overwriting the full dataset.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data_new <- data_new[,-c(4,5,6,7,8,9,24)]
# "Tuition fees up to date" must also be removed: it is only known after the start of university.
```

# Train / validation / test split

Split into train (60%), validation (20%) and test (20%) sets.

```{r}
data_new$Target=as.factor(data_new$Target)

n=nrow(data_new)

set.seed(1234)

# test set (20% of the data)
select_test = sample(1:n, n * 0.2)
test = as.data.frame(data_new[select_test,])

# Remaining data after removing the test set
remaining_data = data_new[-select_test,]
n_remaining = nrow(remaining_data)

# validation set (about 20% of the total data)
select_validation = sample(1:n_remaining, n_remaining * 0.24971)
validation = as.data.frame(remaining_data[select_validation,])

# Train set (remaining 60%)
train = as.data.frame(remaining_data[-select_validation,])

cat("Training set dimensions: ", dim(train), "\n")
cat("Validation set dimensions: ", dim(validation), "\n")
cat("Test set dimensions: ", dim(test), "\n")
```

Save the prepared data for `02_models.Rmd`.

```{r}
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(data_new = data_new, train = train, validation = validation, test = test),
        "data/prepared_data.rds")
```

# Appendix: exploratory experiments (not used in the final models)

Attempt to fix class imbalance: oversample every class up to the size of the largest one (bootstrap with replacement).
The result (`data_balanced`) was not used for the final models, which use the original 4424 observations.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Assume the dataset is called "data" and the target variable is "Target"
table(data$Target)  # Check the initial class distribution

# Number of observations of the most represented class (Graduate)
n_max <- max(table(data$Target))

# Apply the bootstrap to generate more examples of the less represented classes
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility

data_balanced <- data_new %>%
  group_by(Target) %>%
  sample_n(n_max, replace = TRUE) %>%  
  ungroup()

# Check the new class distribution
table(data_balanced$Target)
```
